findings: No contradictory dose-weight basis or first-five-year screening exemption found across Common Eye, RA and SLE. Significant risk factors preclude automatic deferral.

AAO primary abstract says below 400 mg/day in severe obesity; accessible full-text passages describe an initial maximum of 400 mg/day with specialist exceptions. RA/SLE follow the more conservative abstract wording; Common Eye retains explicit dose caution. These are not a universal authorization for higher weight-based dosing.
Recomputed SLE 68 kg x 5 mg/kg = 340 mg/day; RA 400/60 = 6.6667 mg/kg/day, with a calculated 300 mg/day weight-based limit. Practical schedules remain prescriber-directed.
TB and Common Eye both require prompt action for ethambutol acuity/color changes; Common Eye supplies more detailed label/guideline monitoring frequency.
Glaucoma product-specific two-minute occlusion/five-minute spacing does not conflict with Common Eye exact-product guidance.
BPH retains cataract-surgery history after alpha-blocker discontinuation, consistent with Common Eye.
Antiarrhythmic amiodarone teaching includes ocular surveillance without contradicting Common Eye distinction between asymptomatic deposits and optic neuropathy.
sourceAccess: Search-indexed primary abstract and dosage/risk sections read; direct publisher access remains restricted. Other topic sources are in individual review records.
limitations: This is a scoped ocular-content comparison, not verification of the entirety of every related module.
Seizure module has concurrent unrelated edits; its whole-module clinical review remains separate.
